We used to work together for a long time.
When did you arrive? Let us go, you will tell me everything.

Nagiyev brought him, he is an acquaintance of the chef.
Do you also know him well?
Yes, he taught us in Paris.
And they kicked me out of there back then.
I was recently offered work in Russia.

examples.trans: Hello to everyone in our kitchen!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего себе, какой большой шрам!
examples.trans: Wow, what a big scar!

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.
examples.trans: What do you want? Nothing, we are working.

examples.text: Шеф ничего не знает.
examples.trans: The chef knows nothing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: На нашей кухне день начинается одинаково.
examples.trans: In our kitchen the day begins the same way.

examples.text: Ты обещал мне новое летнее меню.
examples.trans: You promised me a new summer menu.

examples.text: Какое ещё летнее меню, Вика?
examples.trans: What summer menu, Vika?
